method_card.title: How to Plot and Interpret Quadratic Graphs
method_card.content:
A quadratic graph is a U-shaped curve (parabola), \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\). If \(a > 0\) it opens upward (a minimum); if \(a < 0\) it opens downward (a maximum).

The roots are where the curve meets the x-axis (\(y = 0\)); a quadratic has 0, 1 or 2. The turning point is the vertex, and the line of symmetry runs vertically through it. For \(y = (x - p)^2 + q\), the turning point is \((p, q)\) and the line of symmetry is \(x = p\).
method_card.example: Plot \(y = x^2 - 4x + 3\). Roots at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 3\) (where \(y = 0\)); turning point \((2, -1)\), the lowest point. ✔

A positive \(x^2\) term gives a minimum turning point; a negative one gives a maximum.
